positions.title: Leader of the Liberal Party of Australia

sources.title: Hon Angus Taylor MP — Parliamentarian profile
sources.note: Positions: Leader of the Opposition; Member for Hume; elected 2013, re-elected 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025.

sources.title: List of Members, 48th Parliament, 29 September 2026
sources.note: Lists Taylor (Hume, LP) as Leader of the Opposition.

sources.title: Shadow ministerial arrangements
sources.note: Announces the Taylor shadow ministry; Leader of the Opposition: Angus Taylor MP.

notes: Elected Leader of the Liberal Party on 13 February 2026 after a party-room ballot (previously Shadow Minister for Defence, 2025–26, and Shadow Treasurer, 2022–25).

sources.title: Senator the Hon Jane Hume — Parliamentarian profile
sources.note: Positions: Deputy Leader of the Opposition; Senator for Victoria; elected 2016, re-elected 2019 and 2025.

sources.note: Lists Hume (VIC, LP) as Deputy Leader of the Opposition.

sources.title: Deputy Leader's address to the Housing Construction Outlook Breakfast
sources.note: Attributed to Jane Hume as Deputy Leader of the Opposition, Shadow Minister for Employment and Industrial Relations, Shadow Minister for Productivity and Deregulation.

notes: A Liberal Party release of 30 September 2026 also styles her Acting Shadow Minister for Finance; the substantive portfolio is held by another senator, so the acting role is not listed here.

sources.title: Senator James Paterson — Parliamentarian profile
sources.note: Chosen by the Parliament of Victoria on 9.3.2016 to fill a casual vacancy; elected 2016, re-elected 2019 and 2025.

sources.title: James Paterson — Liberal Party team page
sources.note: Shadow Minister for Defence; Senator for Victoria.

sources.note: Paterson promoted to the Defence portfolio.

notes: Entered the Senate in March 2016 via a casual vacancy; first elected in his own right at the 2016 election.

sources.title: Hon Andrew Hastie MP — Parliamentarian profile
sources.note: Member for Canning; elected at a 2015 by-election, re-elected 2016, 2019, 2022 and 2025.

sources.title: Andrew Hastie — Liberal Party team page
sources.note: Shadow Minister for Industry and Sovereign Capability; Federal Member for Canning.

sources.title: Shadow ministerial arrangements
sources.note: Names Hastie Deputy Leader in the House of Representatives and Shadow Minister for Industry and Sovereign Capability.

notes: Returned to the shadow ministry on 17 February 2026 after resigning from it on 3 October 2025. The 'Deputy Leader in the House' role is a party designation not recorded as a formal office on APH.
